_what_this_is: Records the version of each upstream dependency that a human has actually REVIEWED. A test asserts each of these equals the version the build RESOLVED. Every dependency floats to latest at build time, so when upstream publishes, that test goes red and the release gate cannot pass until this file is updated.
_stop_before_you_edit_this_file: Read UPSTREAM-REVIEW.md and follow it. Bumping a version here without doing the review defeats the only mechanism that catches upstream behaviour changes, renamed config keys and changed defaults. None of those are visible to the golden tools/list snapshot, and loadConfig is a bare JSON.parse with no schema validation, so a renamed key is discarded in silence.
_notes_are_not_optional: Every bump records what changed, what was adopted, and what was explicitly declined and why. A decline with a reason is worth as much as an adoption: it stops the same question being re-litigated at the next bump. An empty note is a review that did not happen.
_this_file_is_gated: Not by a prompt. Editing this file is unrestricted; what is gated is the RELEASE. The build regenerates four snapshots from the resolved payload -- tools/list, --help, config.d.ts, browsers.json -- and diffs them, runs the full suite, and asserts that this file adjudicates whatever actually moved and answers every manual re-verification row by name. An entry that ignores what the build observed fails the build. See TESTING.md, 'The upstream-review gate'.
_correction_2026_08_15: An earlier version of the note above said a PreToolUse hook asks a human to approve every edit, and that a sub-agent attempting one is killed silently. Both halves were wrong, and measurement disproved them: under permission_mode 'bypassPermissions' a hook's 'ask' returned to a sub-agent is silently downgraded to ALLOW -- the edit lands unprompted, and the gate was inert against exactly the caller most likely to need it. A sub-agent did die during that work, but not from the hook; the cause is unknown and its transcript was zero bytes. Recorded because a confident wrong explanation is worse than an admitted gap, which is the same rule this file applies to versions.

@playwright/mcp.why_it_matters: Ships in the payload. Its CLI surface and config schema are what BrowserAI generates against, and both change without notice.
@playwright/mcp.notes: Baseline; the charter was researched against this version. 78-entry internal tool registry, 69 maximum ever exposed over MCP (9 are skillOnly), 24 by default. Caps at protocol 2025-11-25. Defaults to channel:chrome and headless:false on Windows -- browserName:chromium must be set explicitly or the bundled tree is never consulted. --output-mode was verified to be a no-op for its entire life.

playwright-core.why_it_matters: Carries the actual tool implementations and the browsers.json that pins the Chromium revision. Arrives as @playwright/mcp's own exact dependency, not as a choice we make.
playwright-core.notes: Baseline. browsers.json pins chromium rev 1237 (152.0.7977.8), which is the browser BrowserAI provisions -- full Chromium in every mode, settled 2026-08-15. The same browsers.json also pins chromium-headless-shell at rev 1237; we do not provision it, and the payload build passes --no-shell. Upstream publishes daily alphas. CORRECTION 2026-08-15: this note previously named chromium-headless-shell as the pinned revision, which was true of an earlier design and became wrong when the shell was dropped. Factual correction to the note only -- reviewed version and date are unchanged, because no new review has happened.

ModelContextProtocol.why_it_matters: The protocol implementation on both sides of the proxy. Its typed layer drops unknown properties and throws on unknown content types, which is correct for a client and lossy for a proxy.
ModelContextProtocol.notes: Baseline. Tier 1 SDK under the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation; day-to-day engineering by the Microsoft .NET team. Declares IsAotCompatible=true on every non-netstandard2.0 target -- the author's claim about their code, not a proof for our usage. Full 2026-07-28 protocol support. Note 2.x drops MTP v1 in the 4.0.0 line of xUnit only; unrelated to this package.

Velopack.why_it_matters: Owns the update path, which is the most hazard-dense section of the charter. Five of its nine documented landmines were hit in production by a shipped product examined for this project rather than avoided.
Velopack.notes: Baseline. That product runs 0.0.1298 (pre-1.0), so nothing learned there transfers without re-verification against 1.2.0.

node.why_it_matters: Bundled in the payload as a single node.exe. A major bump changes size and can change process/stdio behaviour.
node.notes: Reviewed v24.19.0 -> v24.20.0 on 2026-08-27. Same Krypton LTS line, released 2026-08-26, 398 commits, npm 11.19.0. WHAT WAS ADOPTED: the whole patch. The payload was rebuilt so the build's own resolver took it (build/Build-Payload.ps1 -SkipBrowser), and the four golden snapshots then moved by exactly one line -- tools-list.json's own `resolvedFrom.node` stamp. cli-help.txt, config-schema.d.ts and browsers.json are byte-identical, and tools-list.json is byte-identical everywhere else, so the real child's advertised surface under the new runtime is unchanged: 24 default, 69 exposed, 78 internal, 9 skill-only, protocol ceiling 2025-11-25. node.exe grew 92,825,416 -> 93,381,448 b (+556,032); archive node-v24.20.0-win-x64.zip, sha256 6cac9ffbca8f6a47091e4b5c772e0606049c3871cb67d900c0cedde630e545ba; LICENSE still at `node-v24.20.0-win-x64/LICENSE`, 160,555 b. @playwright/mcp and playwright-core re-resolved IDENTICALLY (0.0.79 / 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-05) and build/payload/package-lock.json came back byte for byte, so nothing unreviewed rode in on the rebuild, and tool-verdicts.json's `judgedAgainst` -- which names that pair and not node -- does not move. HOW IT WAS READ: this product uses node.exe for exactly two things, running @playwright/mcp's cli.js over stdio pipes and running `cli.js install-browser`, so the release was read against those rather than as a whole. NOTHING AT ALL landed in `process`, `stdio` or `tty`. DECLINED, each with its reason: (1) npm 11.17.0 -> 11.19.0 -- the payload extracts only node.exe and LICENSE from the archive, and the build resolves the JS tree with the BUILD MACHINE's npm.cmd, so the bundled npm ships nowhere and resolves nothing; (2) the 61 `quic` commits -- unreachable from anything here; (3) the 68 `stream` commits -- overwhelmingly the new experimental node:stream/iter, which playwright-core does not use, and the few classic-stream items that could touch a piped child (`Readable.toWeb` termination, setEncoding after buffered data) are covered by the real-child and smoke tiers rather than by reading them; (4) `--permission-audit`, `permission.drop`, wasm JSPI and `--use-system-ca` becoming per-env -- none is on a path BrowserAI takes, and NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH are refused at ChildEnvironment.Refused so no new CLI flag can arrive through the environment; (5) the five node:sqlite fixes -- node:sqlite is NOT this product's SQLite. Node also updated its own bundled amalgamation to 3.53.4, the same number as the pin in third-party/sqlite, and that is a COINCIDENCE and nothing more: BrowserAI's SQLite is compiled into the AOT binary by build/Sqlite.targets and no build resolves Node's. WATCHED, AND CLEARED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY READING: `loader: implement package maps` (SEMVER-MINOR) and `loader: enforce path normalization before lookup` change module resolution, which is how cli.js and the whole payload node_modules tree are found -- the evidence they changed nothing here is the tools-list snapshot itself, produced by running cli.js under this exact node.exe and reading its real tools/list. `crypto: update root certificates to NSS 3.125` is the one item with a live failure mode, because provisioning downloads from Playwright's CDN over TLS and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS is on the inherit list; it is exercised by the first-run provisioning arm rather than asserted separately. `fs: fix cp symlink and EEXIST handling on Windows` and `src: fix libuv assertion on windows` are the release's two Windows fixes and sit in the class rows 2 and 2b watch. RE-VERIFICATION (kb/re-verification.md), every row a Node move puts in play, answered by name: row 2 and row 2b (job containment end to end, and from the published NativeAOT binary) -- ANSWERED GREEN by the gate, JobContainmentTests / JobObjectTests / VerticalSliceTests.KillingThePublishedBinaryLeavesNoNodeAndNoBrowser all pass under v24.20.0; row 21 (payload sizes) -- the two PAYLOAD rows were re-measured by this build and node.exe's figure is updated above, the browser download and provisioning timings are NOT in play because the Chromium revision did not move; row 26 (payload licensing as shipped) -- re-read, Node's LICENSE is still the single aggregated file and the payload's licensing composition is unchanged; row 46 (Node's LICENSE is not published beside node.exe, and the extraction is keyed on the archive path) -- ANSWERED by the build, which found and extracted `node-v24.20.0-win-x64/LICENSE` and would have thrown had the archive been restructured; row 49 (npm lock keying, and `npm ci` not rewriting the lock) -- ANSWERED, the rebuild parsed the lock with -AsHashtable and npm ci left it byte-identical; row 50 (PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD gates only the postinstall paths) -- NOT exercised, this was a -SkipBrowser build, and it is unchanged in any case because playwright-core did not move; row 85 (the update lane's own numbers) -- OWED AND NOT RUN, and the kb entry says so in place, dated, naming the +556,032 b that triggered it. Re-running it needs two real release publishes plus an install, which the row itself calls manual-and-must-be and which this review-and-records batch did not do. NOT ONE FIGURE WAS ADJUSTED: the new shipped total is not the old one plus the delta, because vpk recompresses and the delta is computed against a different full package, so arithmetic would have produced a measured-looking number nobody measured. The entry states the owed re-check in words rather than with the [STALE] token, because RecordedCountTests.NoKnowledgeBaseArticleCarriesAStaleMarker asserts unconditionally that no kb article carries it -- a guard defect worth its own decision, recorded in the entry. Rows 16 and 16a are NOT in play: their trigger is an SDK change to the discover probe, not a Node move. Row 102 is NOT in play: it turns on the @playwright/mcp bump that carries microsoft/playwright#42288, and that pair did not move. v26 is Current rather than LTS and its node.exe is ~10 MB larger. Ship Node's full LICENSE with the payload -- it aggregates OpenSSL, ICU, V8, zlib and c-ares terms.

_chromium_is_derived: Chromium, ffmpeg and winldd revisions are NOT listed here. They follow from the resolved playwright-core's browsers.json and are recorded in the release's resolved-set manifest instead. Reviewing playwright-core covers them.
